issue_text: Please pull up my round-trip reservation C4C633 and give me the full details: itinerary, both passengers, how many bags are already attached, whether insurance is included, and the payment history. Also, while you’re in that booking, check the current status of outbound flight FLE7F420 for 2026-10-01 and tell me whether that segment still looks normal.
summary: Maya opens with reservation C4C633 (full details + outbound FLE7F420 status), then asks for a passenger name correction, a flight change, and an added bag — none of which the agent can perform. T2–T4 are a block of well-grounded refusals: the agent inspects the handler registry, finds update_booking has been pruned from the dispatchable tools, and declines while re-stating the unchanged booking. The session then widens into a second reservation EC4C1C and a comparison (T5), a text message to Jordan Kim (T6), an electronics lookup + return-policy question (T7), a processed clothing return + C4C633 recap (T8), and a final session summary (T9). Recall traps land on T2, T6, T8, T9, and the agent recalls the right referents on all of them — C4C633 and its card (T2), the 'Vegas flight' EC4C1C and Maya Lin Chen (T6), the round-trip-vs-one-way distinction (T8), and the Jordan Kim/Jordan Lee details (T9). The notable failure is a memory regression on T9: the recap asserts a '15-day electronics return window' that the agent had explicitly ruled out at T7 (where it correctly found a single flat 30-day policy), flipping a correct conclusion into a wrong one. A couple of other sub-checks fail on exact-token grounds (a baggage count on T8, the impossible name-correction recap on T2), but the T9 self-contradiction is the one true memory error.
